channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Valdemar Costa Neto: com Flávio eleito, Bolsonaro estará com a gente no dia seguinte
item.description: PL leader Valdemar Costa Neto claimed that Flávio Bolsonaro's election to the presidency would lead to Jair Bolsonaro's release, who is currently ineligible and under house arrest. The statement strengthens the PL's alliance with the former president.

item.title: Lula e Flávio aparecem empatados em 41% no segundo turno, diz Quaest
item.description: A Quaest poll released on September 7 shows that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) are tied at 41% in a hypothetical 2026 presidential runoff.

item.title: Quaest: Lula e Flávio empatam com 41% no segundo turno; Cury vai de 10% para 8% no primeiro
item.description: The Quaest poll shows Lula and Flávio tied at 41% in the second round, while Cury drops from 10% to 8%. Psychiatrist Augusto Cury (Avante) decreased slightly within the margin of error in the latest round of the survey.

item.title: Rejeição a Flávio Bolsonaro é de 55% e a Lula, de 53%, aponta pesquisa Quaest
item.description: Quaest survey reveals significant voter rejection for both Lula (53%) and Flávio Bolsonaro (55%), remaining stable since September. Both candidates face distrust, highlighting pre-election polarization ahead of 2026.

item.title: Flávio usa ato de 7 de Setembro para transformar ações contra Moraes em combustível de campanha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro leveraged the September 7th event on Paulista Avenue to turn revelations involving Alexandre de Moraes and Daniel Vorcaro into campaign fuel. With less than a month before the first round, the senator aims to mobilize his base and attack the Supreme Court minister's image. The strategy seeks to highlight actions against alleged judicial influence in politics.

item.title: Quaest: 33% dizem que a renda não aumentou no último ano e 21%, que subiu menos que o custo de vida
item.description: Quaest poll shows 33% of Brazilians say household income did not increase last year, while 21% report it rose less than the cost of living. Lula leads with 36% of first-round voting intentions, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 29%. Income perception significantly influences voting: Lula leads among those saying income rose more than cost of living (76%), while Flávio leads among those saying income did not increase (34%).

item.title: Boneco inflável de Trump segura Lula preso em ato na Paulista
item.description: A São Paulo protest attended by an estimated 34,200 people, organized by Flávio Bolsonaro, featured an inflatable Trump doll holding a prisoner-style Lula figure. The event intensified attacks on the Supreme Court following leaked messages between Daniel Vorcaro and Minister Moraes.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vai focar em segurança pública e aumento do custo de vida
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro focuses on public security and rising cost of life as key campaign themes, criticizing the Lula government. A Genial/Quaest survey shows a technical tie between the two candidates in the second round, with 41% of voting intentions each.

item.title: Alcolumbre prega união enquanto é pressionado por impeachment de Moraes
item.description: Davi Alcolumbre, president of the Senate, advocated for dialogue and unity during an event attended by Lula, Fachin, and Moraes, while facing pressure to initiate impeachment proceedings against Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. Meanwhile, allies of Bolsonaro, including Nikolas Ferreira and Flávio Bolsonaro, organized protests demanding Moraes' removal.

item.title: Ato de Flávio na Paulista mira Lula e mostra união do bolsonarismo contra pizza no STF
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro held the largest rally of his campaign on Paulista Avenue, leveraging the Vorcaro message scandal and the Banco Master case to directly attack Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and unify the far-right against the STF. The event emphasized criticism of Minister Alexandre de Moraes and called for independent investigations, aiming to counteract leaks and judicial actions that could damage his candidacy.

item.title: Quaest: Lula lidera no primeiro turno com 36% contra Flávio que registra 29%
item.description: A September 2026 Quaest poll shows President Lula (PT) leading with 36% of voting intentions, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) at 29%. The survey interviewed 2,004 people between September 3 and 6, with a 2 percentage point margin of error.

item.title: Fernanda Bolsonaro usa jaqueta de R$ 999 em ato na Paulista
item.description: Fernanda Bolsonaro wore a Zara leather jacket costing R$999 at the September 7th demonstration on Paulista Avenue, alongside PL presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro. The rally featured criticism of Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes and drew fewer attendees compared to previous years.

item.title: Rejeição a Lula se mantém em 53%, e a de Flávio Bolsonaro vai a 55%, mostra Quaest
item.description: Rejection of President Lula remains at 53%, while Flávio Bolsonaro's rises to 55%, according to a Genial/Quaest survey. The variation is within the two percentage point margin of error.

item.title: Quaest: 32% dizem que Lula e PT vencerem é o melhor resultado da eleição presidencial; para 24%, a volta da família Bolsonaro
item.description: A Quaest survey shows 32% of Brazilians view Lula and PT winning as the best electoral outcome in 2026, while 24% prefer the return of the Bolsonaro family. With a two-point margin of error, the data reveals regional divides, with stronger PT support in the Northeast and Bolsonaro backing in the South.

item.title: Quaest: 50% desaprovam o governo Lula e 43% aprovam, aponta pesquisa
item.description: A Quaest poll released on September 7 shows that 50% of Brazilians disapprove of President Lula's government, while 43% approve. The survey was conducted between September 3 and 6, during the STF crisis, with a margin of error of two percentage points and 95% confidence.

item.title: Ação contra lei que beneficiou filho de Arthur Lira fracassa no STF
item.description: Minister Cármen Lúcia of the STF rejected a lawsuit filed by the Democracia Cristã party against a law modifying the minimum age verification rules for elected candidates, which benefited Alvinho Lira (son of Arthur Lira). The STF did not address the case's merits due to the party's lack of representation in Congress, keeping the legislation valid.

item.title: Quaest: Lula e Flávio empatam numericamente no segundo turno
item.description: Lula and Flávio tie at 41% in hypothetical runoff vote, according to Quaest poll conducted September 3-6. Both held steady from the previous round.

item.title: Ato de Flávio Bolsonaro na av. Paulista vira protesto contra Moraes e reúne quase 30 mil: 'Última semana me fez estar aqui'
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's event on Paulista Avenue turned into a protest against Minister Alexandre de Moraes, gathering around 30,000 people. The mobilization, organized by allies of former President Jair Bolsonaro, had lower attendance than similar events from the previous year. Flávio stated that the "last week" motivated him to take part in the demonstration.

item.title: Análise: 'A parada de Sete de Setembro e o calcanhar de Aquiles de Lula', escreve Felipe Nunes, diretor da Quaest
item.description: Quaest survey shows a technical tie between Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro in the second round, each getting 41%, while Lula leads the first round with 36% against 29% for the Bolsonarist candidate. This symmetry reflects Brazilian polarization, with balanced fears about both returning to power.

item.title: Quaest: Lula tem 36% no primeiro turno; Flávio, 29%
item.description: The Quaest survey in September shows Lula at 36% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 29% in the first round, maintaining stable voting intentions. Other candidates like Augusto Cury (8%) and Ronaldo Caiado (3%) remain with low representation. The inclusion of Pablo Marçal does not significantly alter the results.

item.title: Aprovação do governo Lula vai a 43% e desaprovação chega a 50% em meio à crise do STF
item.description: Government approval for Lula dropped to 43%, while disapproval reaches 50% amid the STF crisis involving Alexandre de Moraes and the Master case. The Quaest survey shows the deterioration of the president's image, with a negative balance of seven points, and the polarized electoral scenario favors Lula, who leads with 36% of voting intentions in the first round.

item.title: Assista à íntegra de todos os discursos no ato de Flávio na Paulista
item.description: On Monday, September 7, 2026, right-wing demonstrations on Paulista Avenue in São Paulo gathered supporters of Flávio Bolsonaro and Romeu Zema to protest against President Lula and Minister Moraes. The PL rally, with the slogan 'Out with Lula, Out with Moraes,' featured speeches from allies criticizing the Supreme Court and the federal government. Tensions escalated following the release of messages from the founder of Banco Master to Minister Moraes.

item.title: Lula lidera pesquisa Quaest no 1º turno com 36%, contra 29% de Flávio; Cury marca 8%
item.description: A Quaest survey commissioned by Globo shows Lula leading the first round with 36%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 29% and Augusto Cury at 8%. In a simulated second round, the top two candidates are tied. Pablo Marçal, convicted and ineligible, is mentioned but with low projection.

item.title: Quaest: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro empatam com 41% no 2º turno
item.description: Quaest poll released on September 7 shows a technical tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro at 41% each in the 2nd round, within the margin of error. Lula leads the 1st round with 36%, followed by Flávio at 29%. The survey of 2,004 voters was conducted between September 3 and 6, with a two-point margin of error.

item.title: Quaest: pesquisa mostra Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro empatados no 2º turno
item.description: The latest Quaest poll, commissioned by O GLOBO and TV Globo, shows a technical tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical second round, both at 41%, within a 2-point margin of error. In the first round, Lula leads with 36% followed by Flávio at 29%, while other candidates trail behind. The survey was conducted after internal disputes at the STF, but does not directly reflect the political issues mentioned.

item.title: Quaest: 50% desaprovam e 43% aprovam governo Lula
item.description: A Quaest poll shows 50% disapprove of President Lula's government, with 43% approving, reflecting the largest gap between approval and disapproval since he took office. Economic perception remains negative, with 49% of voters saying the country's situation has worsened in the last 12 months.

item.title: Quaest: Lula lidera com 36% no 1º turno; Flávio tem 29% e Cury marca 8%
item.description: The latest Quaest poll shows Lula leading with 36% in the first round, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro (29%) and Augusto Cury (8%). The survey was conducted between September 3-6 with 2,004 respondents and a ±2 point margin of error.

item.title: Quaest, 2º turno: Lula, 41%; Flávio Bolsonaro, 41%
item.description: A Quaest poll commissioned by Globo shows a technical tie between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the second round, both at 41%, with 13% of blank, null, and non-voters. Lula holds more comfortable margins against other candidates like Caiado (PSD) and Zema (Novo), at 41% and 44% support respectively.

item.title: Governo e setor produtivo esperam voltar a exportar frango e mel em até dois meses
item.description: Following an EU audit, the Lula government and the productive sector hope to resume poultry and honey exports to the European bloc within two months, optimistically aiming to restart sales before the electoral runoff.

item.title: Manifestação de Flávio Bolsonaro na Paulista reuniu 28,5 mil pessoas; público encolheu desde 2022
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's demonstration on Paulista Avenue, held on Independence Day, gathered 28,500 people according to the USP/Cebrap Monitor and More in Common, representing a decline compared to 2022 and 2024. The rally gained momentum after revelations about conversations between Minister Alexandre de Moraes and banker Daniel Vorcaro, with critiques of the Supreme Court central to the event.

item.title: Manifestação de 7 de Setembro na Avenida Paulista reúne candidatos ao governo de São Paulo, Rio e Paraná
item.description: September 7th demonstration on Paulista Avenue, led by Flávio Bolsonaro, gathered gubernatorial candidates from São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and Paraná, with criticism directed at Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. Tarcísio de Freitas spoke, while Douglas Ruas and Sergio Moro attended without delivering speeches.

item.title: USP estima 28.500 em ato de Flávio na avenida Paulista
item.description: The September 7th rally on Paulista Avenue in São Paulo gathered 28,500 people according to USP/Cebrap estimates, peaking between 25,100 and 32,000. Organized by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), the event targeted criticism at President Lula and Minister Moraes, though it fell short of the 100,000 goal and the 48,800 attendees recorded the previous year.

item.title: No ápice, ato com Flávio Bolsonaro reúne 28,5 mil pessoas na Paulista, aponta metodologia da USP
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) campaign rally on Paulista Avenue in São Paulo drew 28,5 thousand people at its peak, according to USP/Cebrap methodology. The event featured public security and health proposals, along with criticism of the Supreme Federal Court and Minister Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Duelo do 7/9 traz Flávio no ataque e Lula na defesa
item.description: In the opposition-proposed debate, Flávio attacked Lula over the institutional crisis at the STF, while Lula defended his administration. Both used the same issue to position their campaigns in the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Ato de 7 de Setembro de Flávio leva 28,5 mil pessoas à Paulista, aponta USP; em 2025 foram 42,2 mil
item.description: The September 7th rally convened by Flávio Bolsonaro on Paulista Avenue gathered 28,500 people, according to USP/Cebrap and More in Common, with a margin of error of 3,400. The number is lower than the 42,200 recorded at the same event in 2025 and the 45,400 in 2024. The count was conducted using aerial photos analyzed with artificial intelligence.

item.title: USP: comício de Flávio Bolsonaro na Paulista tem pico de 28,5 mil pessoas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's rally on Paulista Avenue on September 7 gathered around 28,500 people, according to USP estimates, below previous editions. The count was conducted using AI from 12 aerial photos.

item.title: Assista à íntegra do discurso de Flávio Bolsonaro na Paulista
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro spoke in São Paulo criticizing Lula and Morais, announcing Supreme Court nominations, and warning about a supposed 'third stab' against his campaign. He emphasized alliances and labeled the minister a 'bad orange'.

item.title: Quando a escolha é pelo menos mau
item.description: The analysis questions whether voters choose based on affection or repulsion towards candidates, noting that high rejection rates in Brazil suggest a climate of aversion. Electoral behavior appears driven more by negative emotions than positive convictions.

item.title: Paulo Vieira acompanha desfile de 7 de Setembro na tribuna de Lula
item.description: Paulo Vieira attended the September 7th civic-military parade from the presidential gallery, alongside officials and President Lula, and later joined Lula and First Lady Janja for lunch. His appearance follows months after he portrayed Lula during the Rio Carnival, representing the president in a tribute by the Acadêmicos de Niterói.

item.title: Nikolas marca ato no Amapá para pressionar Alcolumbre a pautar impeachment
item.description: Federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) announced a protest in Amapá to pressure Senate president Davi Alcolumbre to schedule the impeachment of Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. During a rally on Paulista Avenue, Nikolas criticized Alcolumbre and reaffirmed support for Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 presidential candidacy.

item.title: “Divulgaram luta contra o STF e terminaram farmando aura com ladrão”
item.description: Renan Santos criticized Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's performance at a São Paulo protest, using the phrase 'farming aura' to describe the rapprochement between allies who previously opposed the Supreme Court. The post was published on social media X and highlighted tensions within the Brazilian opposition. The incident reflects the polarized and uncertain alliance landscape in the 2026 pre-campaign.

item.title: Zema é hostilizado na Paulista: “Veio se aproveitar da manifestação?”
item.description: Presidential candidate Romeu Zema (Novo-MG) was confronted by a protester during a demonstration on Paulista Avenue in São Paulo, who questioned whether he was trying to take advantage of Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) event. Zema attended a rally organized by his party, focusing on criticism of Lula and Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, without mobilizing supporters or livestreaming, unlike Flávio. The footage shows the candidate being ignored by the protester, with a security guard intervening at the end.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que é preciso ‘proteger o STF de Alexandre de Moraes’
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro stated at a Paulista Avenue rally that it is necessary to protect the STF from Alexandre de Moraes, criticizing the minister and promising to appoint five new justices. He also advocated for declaring war on drug traffickers and lowering the age of criminal responsibility.

item.title: O tamanho do público do ato de Flávio Bolsonaro na Avenida Paulista, segundo a USP
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-SP) gathered 28,500 people on Paulista Avenue for Independence Day, according to USP/Cebrap research. Writer Augusto Cury (Avante) drew 1,400 people at Copacabana, while President Lula attended an institutional event in Brasília with an official estimate of 70,000 attendees.

item.title: Flávio elenca promessas, critica o governo e diz que ‘votar em Lula é votar em Moraes’
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro spoke on Paulista Avenue, criticizing Lula and Moraes, promising increased security and Supreme Court appointments. He also praised the previous government and warned about potential attacks.

item.title: Flávio diz que ‘quem vota em Lula, vota em Moraes’ e fala em encerrar ‘consórcio’ entre eles
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro claimed that Lula voters indirectly support Moraes during a campaign rally on Paulista Avenue. He accused the president of using the Supreme Court to target Bolsonaro supporters and promised to appoint five justices, including Moraes' removal. He also pledged to fight gender ideology in schools and restore judicial credibility.

item.title: Nikolas anuncia ato contra Alcolumbre no Amapá
item.description: Federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL) announced a rally in Amapá against Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, demanding the impeachment of Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. During the September 7th demonstration on Paulista Avenue in São Paulo, organized by Flávio Bolsonaro, criticisms rose against the Supreme Court and President Lula's government. Leaked messages between Daniel Vorcaro and Moraes intensified Flávio's attacks on the minister.

item.title: Ato na Paulista reaproxima Tarcísio, Nikolas e Malafaia da campanha de Flávio com ataques a Moraes e críticas ao PT
item.description: The right-wing rally on Paulista Avenue brought Tarcísio, Nikolas, and Malafaia closer to Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, with speeches supporting the candidate and attacking Alexandre de Moraes and the PT.

item.title: Ato na Paulista tem Trump segurando boneco de Lula e bandeiras dos EUA
item.description: A protest on Paulista Avenue, organized by Bolsonaro supporters, included criticism of the STF, praise for ministers, and controversial symbols such as a Trump doll holding a Lula puppet. The rally featured Tarcísio de Freitas and Nikolas Ferreira but did not center Flávio Bolsonaro as the main figure.

item.title: Vou indicar 5 ministros ao STF porque Moraes vai cair, afirma Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro stated he intends to appoint five ministers to the STF following the anticipated fall of Alexandre de Moraes, during a protest against Lula and Moraes on Paulista Avenue. He harshly criticized the minister, calling him 'bad orange' and accusing the Supreme Court of persecuting political opponents.
